name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
principle: Concurrent code accesses a shared resource without enforcing exclusive or atomic access. Another thread, process, or signal handler can modify the resource during the timing window, corrupting state or bypassing security checks.
detection_signals: read-modify-write on shared state such as x++, balance = balance - amount, map.put(...) without mutex, synchronized, Lock, or atomic API
global, static, singleton, or heap object written from multiple threads without pthread_mutex_t, std::mutex, synchronized, java.util.concurrent.locks.Lock, or std::atomic/Atomic*
check-then-use file pattern access()/stat()/lstat()/File.exists() followed by open()/fopen()/unlink()/FileInputStream on the same path
pthread_mutex_lock(), pthread_mutex_trylock(), mtx_lock(), or lock acquisition return value ignored before shared-resource access
Java check-then-act on shared collection or field such as if (!map.containsKey(k)) map.put(k,v) without ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent or synchronization
database SELECT/read of balance, quota, or state followed by separate UPDATE/write without transaction, row lock, or atomic UPDATE predicate
signal handler reads/writes global state or calls malloc(), free(), printf(), or other non-async-signal-safe functions
negative_signals: entire read-check-write sequence is inside the same mutex/monitor/Lock critical section and lock acquisition failure is handled
shared counter/state uses atomic_int, std::atomic, AtomicInteger, AtomicReference, compareAndSet, fetch_add, or synchronized accessor
file creation/open uses atomic flags such as open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL), O_NOFOLLOW with fstat() after open, mkstemp(), or atomic rename()
database read-validate-write is inside one transaction with SELECT FOR UPDATE or a single conditional UPDATE statement
shared data is thread_local, ThreadLocal, stack-local, or otherwise not shared across concurrent executions
code path is provably single-threaded, single-process, and has no signal/interrupt handler touching the resource
false_defense_traps: declaring shared variables volatile instead of using locks or atomic operations
double-checked locking without correct memory-ordering or Java volatile
checking a file path with access()/stat()/exists() before opening the same path
using thread-safe individual calls while composing non-atomic check-then-act sequences
locking only the write but leaving related reads or validation outside the same critical section
verification_focus: Can two concurrent executions observe or change the same resource between a security-relevant check/read and its dependent use/write without one atomic synchronization boundary?

consequence_chains.trigger: path or permission is checked before a later file use
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker swaps the resource and bypasses authorization or modifies the wrong file

consequence_chains.trigger: race bypasses cleanup or triggers repeated initialization
consequence_chains.consequence: CPU, memory, handle, or other resource exhaustion

consequence_chains.trigger: race combines predictable pathname with loose permissions or symlink replacement
consequence_chains.consequence: read or overwrite unintended files and application data

patch_principle: Wrap the complete critical sequence in a mutex, monitor, Lock, transaction, or other synchronization primitive.
Use atomic operations or thread-safe abstractions for shared variables and collections; do not split check and update.
Remove shared mutable state where possible by using thread-local data, immutable objects, message passing, or ownership transfer.
For file TOCTOU, avoid path check-then-use; open/create atomically and validate the opened descriptor with fstat().
For database state, use one transaction with row locks or a single conditional atomic UPDATE.
